title: YouTube AdSense India Taxes: W-8BEN Guide to 15% Rate
summary: Indian creators: Cut YouTube AdSense US withholding with W-8BEN. Guide to YouTube earnings tax withholding in India, treaty rate (15%), and YouTube tax forms.
body_text: Key takeaways Google withholds US tax on earnings from US viewers, without tax info the backup rate can be up to 24% on your total worldwide revenue. File Form W-8BEN in AdSense, claim India’s treaty under Article 12, and the US withholding drops to 15% on your US sourced revenue only. Your PAN works as your Foreign TIN, most Indian creators do not need an ITIN to claim the treaty rate. Choose Article 12, Royalties, enter 15%, and certify Indian tax residency to activate the treaty benefits. W-8BEN is typically valid for about three years, set a reminder to refresh it before expiry. Download Form 1042-S each year and claim Foreign Tax Credit in India by filing Form 67 before your ITR deadline. Verify that only US revenue is being withheld by checking AdSense Payments → Transactions, adjust if numbers look off. Cut FX spreads and bank fees on payouts, and secure e-FIRA for compliance by using purpose built tools such as Karbon Business. Avoid common mistakes, wrong form type, missing PAN, US address, expired W-8BEN, and not checking reports. For payout mechanics, fees, and proofs, see AdSense payouts to India explained in this guide on YouTube AdSense India . Understanding US withholding on YouTube earnings Google applies US withholding on income from US viewers, this includes ads, YouTube Premium, Super Chat, memberships, and similar features. This is separate from Indian taxes, and separate from AdSense platform fees. If you do not submit tax information, Google can apply backup withholding of up to 24% on your total global earnings, not just the portion from US viewers. With a valid W-8BEN and the India treaty rate, withholding falls to 15% and applies only to the US sourced slice. For background and policy context, see this TaxGuru explainer on YouTube creator withholding . Bottom line: File your tax form, claim the treaty, and the US takes a smaller percentage, only from US viewers, letting you keep more of your hard earned income. The India US tax treaty and why it matters The India US Double Tax Avoidance Agreement prevents the same income from being taxed twice. Under Article 12, royalties, which include YouTube ad revenue, Indian residents can claim a 15% treaty rate on the US sourced portion. If you skip the treaty claim, the default US rate can be 30% on your US earnings, and if you provide no tax info at all, backup withholding of up to 24% can hit your entire global payout. The treaty only applies to US audience revenue, income from viewers in India or any non US country is not subject to US withholding. This is why filing the right YouTube tax forms in AdSense is so valuable. For additional industry coverage, see Economic Times on YouTube tax rules for Indian creators . Step by step, how to file YouTube tax forms W 8BEN in AdSense Step 1: Navigate to tax settings Log in to AdSense. Go to Payments, then Manage settings, find United States tax info, and click Add tax info. Step 2: Select the correct form Choose W-8BEN if you are an individual creator. If you operate as a registered entity, company or LLP, you will use W-8BEN-E instead, see this quick guide to W-8BEN and W-8BEN-E . Most solo creators should select W-8BEN. Step 3: Part I, personal information Enter your legal name as per PAN, select India as your country of citizenship and tax residency, and provide your Indian residential address. Avoid using any US address unless you are actually a US tax resident. Step 4: Part II, tax identification and treaty Enter your PAN as the Foreign TIN. Tick Claim tax treaty benefits, select India, choose Article 12, Royalties, and enter 15% as the treaty rate. Step 5: Part III, certifications and signature Read and sign to certify that you are an Indian tax resident, that details are accurate, and you are entitled to the treaty rate. Sign electronically and submit. Step 6: Submit, confirm, and monitor After submission, Google confirms by email, typically within hours. The new rate applies immediately or from the next cycle. W-8BEN is usually valid for about three years, update early if your situation changes. Verify withholding under Payments → Transactions in AdSense, if numbers look off, review your filing or raise a ticket. For further reference, see the TaxGuru walkthrough . Real world examples, how much you save by filing W 8BEN Assume monthly YouTube revenue is $1,000, of which $100 is from US viewers. Using ₹84 per $1 as an illustration: Scenario 1, no form filed: 24% on total $1,000, withholding $240, net $760. Scenario 2, W-8BEN with treaty: 15% on $100 only, withholding $15, net $985. Scenario 3, W-8BEN without treaty: 30% on $100, withholding $30, net $970. Scenario 4, zero US viewers: Withholding $0, regardless of total earnings. The difference is stark, even with modest US viewership, the treaty filing keeps thousands of rupees in your pocket each month. Common mistakes that increase YouTube earnings tax withholding Not filing any form: Triggers backup withholding, up to 24% on total worldwide earnings. Choosing the wrong form: Individuals must use W-8BEN, entities use W-8BEN-E, wrong selections cause delays or higher rates. Missing or incorrect PAN: PAN is your Foreign TIN, typos or blanks can invalidate benefits. Using a US address: May push you toward W-9 and US person treatment, avoid unless true. Letting W-8BEN expire: After expiry, Google reverts to backup withholding, renew on time. Not checking reports: Always confirm the rate under Payments → Transactions. Understanding Form 1042 S and AdSense reports Google issues Form 1042 S annually, usually by March, if any US tax was withheld. It shows your US sourced income, the tax withheld, and the rate applied. Download it from Payments → Tax documents, store it safely, and use it while filing your Indian return to claim Foreign Tax Credit via Form 67. Box 2: Income code, usually 16 for royalties. Box 7a: Gross income paid, US sourced. Box 7b: Tax withheld. Box 12a: Tax rate, 15% if treaty applied. Reporting YouTube income and claiming tax credits in India YouTube income is business income in India. Report it in your ITR, pay tax per slab, or consider presumptive taxation if eligible. The US withholding does not auto reduce Indian tax, you must claim Foreign Tax Credit by filing Form 67 before filing ITR. Keep these documents ready, AdSense statements, Form 1042 S, bank statements, and e FIRA or FIRC for each inward remittance. Your CA will compute eligible FTC to prevent double taxation. Managing international payments and FX for YouTube creators AdSense typically pays Indian creators by bank transfer. Traditional routes can carry hidden FX spreads and intermediary fees, which quietly reduce your INR credit. Tools purpose built for international receipts can help you receive via local rails like ACH, SEPA, or FPS, which are faster and often cheaper than SWIFT, then settle INR quickly with clean compliance records. What to compare when choosing a solution: Karbon Business : Virtual USD, GBP, EUR, CAD accounts, local collection, transparent 1% fee, zero FX markup, INR in 24 to 48 hours, automatic e FIRA generation. Wise Business: Multi currency accounts, transparent pricing, wide coverage. Payoneer: Marketplace friendly, broad compatibility. PayPal Business: Ubiquitous, usually higher FX markups. Razorpay X International: India focused, SME friendly. Goal: maximize take home after withholding, after FX, and after Indian taxes, while staying audit ready. Quick checklist for Indian YouTube creators File W-8BEN with PAN, claim India treaty at 15% under Article 12, royalties. Confirm that withholding applies only to US viewers by reviewing AdSense Transactions. Download annual Form 1042 S, store it with monthly statements and bank credits. File Form 67 before ITR to claim Foreign Tax Credit, avoid double tax. Maintain e FIRA or FIRC for each inward remittance to build a clean audit trail. Set a reminder to renew your W-8BEN every three years, or when details change. Use payment solutions with transparent FX and automated compliance, such as Karbon Business . Work with a qualified CA as income scales, especially for GST or audit thresholds. Final thoughts Understanding YouTube earnings tax withholding in India is essential if you want to keep more of your revenue. File W-8BEN, claim the treaty, and your effective US tax can drop from backup rates on total income to just 15% on the US slice. Keep immaculate records, monitor AdSense reports, pick cost effective payout rails, and claim FTC in India to stay compliant and maximize income. If you have not filed W-8BEN yet, do it today, the minutes you invest can pay you back every single month. FAQ YouTube tax ka withholding India me kya hota hai, kitna percent katega? YouTube par US viewers se jo income aata hai, uspe Google US tax withhold karta hai, agar aap tax forms submit nahi karte to backup rate 24% tak total earnings par lag sakta hai, par W-8BEN file karke India US treaty claim karein to sirf US sourced revenue par 15% katega. Main individual YouTuber hoon, W-8BEN bharu ya W-8BEN-E? Individual creators ke liye W-8BEN sahi form hai, W-8BEN-E entities, jaise company ya LLP ke liye hota hai, agar aap future me entity banate hain, tab W-8BEN vs W-8BEN-E guide dekhkar switch karein. Treaty claim ke liye ITIN chahiye kya, PAN chalega? Aksar cases me ITIN ki zarurat nahi hoti, Google Indian creators ke liye PAN ko Foreign TIN ke roop me accept karta hai, isliye PAN number sahi dalna zaruri hai. W-8BEN me kaunsa article select karna hai, aur rate kya likhna hai? Treaty benefits claim karte waqt Article 12, Royalties choose karein, aur rate me 15% enter karein, India ko treaty country select karna na bhoolein. W-8BEN kab expire hota hai, renew kaise karu? Form aam taur par lagbhag teen saal ke liye valid rehta hai, expiry ke pehle AdSense me jaakar refresh karein, warna Google backup withholding par chala jaata hai, calendar reminder zarur set karein. Agar mere US viewers zero hain to tax withhold hoga kya? Nahi, US viewers zero hone par US withholding zero hota hai, par phir bhi W-8BEN file karke apni tax residency confirm karna best practice hai, taaki backup withholding kabhi trigger na ho. 1042-S kya hota hai, India me iska use kaise hoga? Form 1042-S Google ka annual US tax statement hai, jisme US sourced income, withhold tax, aur rate diya hota hai, is document ko Form 67 ke saath use karke India me Foreign Tax Credit claim kiya jaata hai, jisse double tax bachta hai. Form 67 kab file karna hota hai, aur kaunse documents chahiye? Form 67 ITR file karne se pehle submit hota hai, aapko AdSense statements, 1042-S, bank statements, aur e-FIRA ya FIRC ki zarurat padegi, in documents se CA aapka eligible FTC compute karta hai. AdSense me kaise check karu ki 15% treaty rate sahi lag raha hai? Payments → Transactions me withholding line items dekhkar verify karein, agar amount zyada lag raha ho to apna W-8BEN submission dubara review karein, aur zarurat par AdSense support se case raise karein. YouTube payout aata hai par bank FX markup me kaafi loss hota hai, kya karu? Traditional bank wires me hidden FX spreads, intermediary fees, aur slow processing ho sakti hai, isliye aap virtual USD, GBP, EUR, CAD accounts ke through local rails par collect karke INR fast settle kara sakte hain, Karbon Business jaise platforms 1% flat fee, zero FX markup, aur automatic e-FIRA dete hain, jo compliance me bhi madad karta hai. PayPal se AdSense ya sponsorship ka paisa lana mehenga padta hai, Karbon Business sasta padega? PayPal me FX markup aur platform fees effective rate ko badha dete hain, jabki Karbon Business local accounts, zero FX markup, aur transparent pricing deta hai, INR 24 se 48 ghanto me credit hota hai, aur e-FIRA bhi milta hai, jo books aur taxes ke liye useful hai. AdSense ke alawa brand sponsorships ka USD payment kaise receive karu, compliance clean rahe? Brand deals ke liye invoice issue karein, sahi RBI purpose code use karein, aur aise platform use karein jo e-FIRA, bank proof, aur tracking de, Karbon Business me virtual accounts par ACH ya SEPA collection possible hota hai, fir INR settlement ke saath audit trail maintain hota hai. Agar US me zyada withholding ho gaya to refund mil sakta hai kya? US refund ke liye US tax return file karna pad sakta hai, jo zyadatar Indian creators ko karna nahi padta, practical approach yeh hai ki India me Form 67 ke through FTC claim karke apni Indian tax liability offset karen. Agar me private limited bana lu to kya W-8BEN-E better hoga aur tax kam hoga? Entity structure change se form type change hota hai, W-8BEN-E entities ke liye sahi hai, lekin treaty rate royalties par 15% hi rehta hai, isliye decision compliance, liability, aur business goals ke basis par lein, sirf withholding optimization ke liye nahi. Payment proofs, e-FIRA, 1042-S, sab maintain kaise karu, audit me problem na aaye? Har payout ke liye bank credit, e-FIRA, AdSense transaction export, aur saal ke end me 1042-S ek folder me rakhein, tools jaise Karbon Business automatic e-FIRA generate karte hain, jisse Form 67 aur ITR filing me data ready milta hai. Agar kal ko treaty rules change ho gaye to kya hoga, mere payouts par impact kaise track karu? Treaty ya platform policy update aane par AdSense email alerts, tax center, aur Transactions ko monitor karein, withholding me unexpected spike dikhe to W-8BEN details re check karein, industry updates padhein, aur zarurat ho to CA se consult karein.

title: Cemtrex Reports Fiscal Year 2026 First Quarter Financial Results
summary: Hauppauge, NY, Feb. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- – Cemtrex, Inc. (Nasdaq: CETX, CETXP) today reported results for the 2026 first fiscal…...
body_text: Cemtrex Reports Fiscal Year 2026 First Quarter Financial Results February 17, 2026 4:15pm EST Download as PDF Related Documents 10-Q Filing PDF HTML XBRL ZIP Hauppauge, NY, Feb. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- – Cemtrex, Inc. (Nasdaq: CETX, CETXP) today reported results for the 2026 first fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2025. Key Highlights for First Fiscal Quarter 2026 Revenues for Q1 ’26 increased 17% to $16.1 million, compared to revenue in the prior year of $13.7 million. Industrial segment revenue increased 28% to $10.6 million, compared to revenue in the prior year of $8.3 million. Security segment revenue increased 1% to $5.5 million, compared to revenue in the prior year of $5.4 million. Cash and cash equivalents increased 312% to $20.5 million, compared to the prior year of $5 million. Management Commentary Cemtrex Chairman and CEO, Saagar Govil, commented on the results: “Fiscal Q1 2026 was a quarter of decisive action. We strengthened our balance sheet, delivered continued revenue growth driven by our Industrial segment. Operating loss for the quarter was $2.8 million, compared to $2.3 million in the prior year period, primarily reflecting lower gross margin in Security and certain one-time expenses, including a write-off of obsolete demo equipment and elevated legal and transaction costs related to acquisition activity and other matters. Excluding these non-recurring items, our focus remains on improving segment contribution and lowering the run-rate cost structure. In Security, we saw gross margin compression driven by tariff related cost pressures and softer demand from certain government and corrections customers during the quarter, which was below typical historical levels amid broader public-sector budget and shutdown-related disruptions. We responded by implementing pricing adjustments and reducing overhead by approximately $2.5 to $3.0 million on an annualized basis, which went into full effect in early Q2. We expect the impact of these actions to be reflected over the coming quarters, and we anticipate one-time restructuring charges in the current fiscal quarter associated with these reductions. Our objective is to restore the Security segment toward its historical gross margin profile over the coming quarters while positioning Vicon as a disciplined, durable earnings platform. Early adoption of our NEXT camera line continues to build, and we remain confident in the long-term competitive positioning of the business. In Industrial, revenue increased 28% to $10.6 million, a record quarter for the segment, reflecting operational discipline and growing demand for our services. We continue to secure infrastructure related projects and enter 2026 with a strong pipeline as we build operating momentum across the platform. During the quarter we materially improved financial flexibility through equity raises and debt settlements, increasing working capital and strengthening our capital structure. Subsequent to quarter end, we completed the acquisitions of Invocon and Richland Industries, expanding our operating footprint and earnings base. Invocon establishes our Aerospace and Defense segment and expands our presence in mission critical engineering markets. Richland strengthens AIS’s geographic reach and fabrication capabilities in the Southeast. Contributions from both acquisitions will begin to be reflected starting in the second fiscal quarter. As we enter the second quarter, the Company expects the combined impact of cost actions in Security and earnings contributions from recently completed acquisitions to improve performance. Our focus for fiscal 2026 is restoring segment margins, expanding operating income, and strengthening cash flow generation across the platform. We remain focused on disciplined execution and capital allocation as we build a diversified platform designed to deliver durable operating income over time. We continue to pursue acquisitions that fit our criteria for durable margins and cash generation.” Condensed Financial Summary (Fiscal Q1 2026) Revenue: $16.1 million Gross profit: $5.6 million Gross margin: 35% Operating loss: $2.8 million Net loss: $20.6 million, primarily driven by non-cash items related to debt settlement Cash and cash equivalents: $20.5 million Additional details are available in the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10 Q filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. About Cemtrex Cemtrex, Inc. (Nasdaq: CETX) is a diversified industrial and technology company operating across the Security, Industrial, and Aerospace & Defense sectors. The Company’s Security segment, led by Vicon Industries, provides advanced video management software, high-performance security cameras, and integrated surveillance solutions for enterprise, government, and critical infrastructure customers. Its Industrial segment, through Advanced Industrial Services (AIS), delivers specialized rigging, millwrighting, process piping, and equipment installation services to manufacturers nationwide. Cemtrex’s Aerospace & Defense segment, anchored by Invocon, provides mission-critical engineering, instrumentation, and sensing solutions supporting aerospace, defense, and space-based programs. With a focus on disciplined execution and strategic growth, Cemtrex is committed to building durable businesses that enhance safety, reliability, and long-term value for its customers and shareholders. For more information, visit www.cemtrex.com . title: Cipher Mining Rebrands as Cipher Digital to Double Down on AI Data Center Leases
summary: Cipher Mining said it has rebranded as Cipher Digital as the company leans further into AI data center development, alongside fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results
body_text: Cipher Mining said it has rebranded as Cipher Digital (NASDAQ: CIFR) as the company leans further into AI data center development, alongside fourth-quarter and full-year 2025 results released Tuesday. The Nasdaq-listed bitcoin miner said the name change is meant to reflect a shift away from a business model centered on bitcoin mining toward one built on long-term data center leases and contracted cash flows. CEO Tyler Page said Cipher expanded its hosted-compute relationships during the quarter, including an upsized lease with Fluidstack and Google and what it described as its first HPC lease with Amazon. As part of that repositioning, Cipher said it sold its 49% interest in three 40-megawatt joint-venture mining sites—Alborz, Bear and Chief—along with select mining rigs previously deployed at its Black Pearl site to Canaan (NASDAQ: CAN) in a $40 million all-stock deal. For the fourth quarter, Cipher reported revenue of $60 million and an adjusted net loss of $55 million. It also reported holding $125.4 million worth of bitcoin as of Dec. 31, which implied that it mined an estimated 623 BTC during the quarter and sold about 690 BTC in total. Cipher noted debt financings that it said can fully fund the construction for two marquee HPC developments, Barber Lake and Black Pearl. Cipher completed three senior secured note offerings totaling $3.73 billion in proceeds, including $1.73 billion at 7.125% for Barber Lake (a $1.4 billion deal plus a $333 million add-on) and $2.0 billion at 6.125% for Black Pearl. On the commercial side, Cipher said it has 600 megawatts of gross contracted HPC capacity across two leases: a 15-year, 300 MW lease with AWS and a 10-year, 300 MW lease with Fluidstack and Google. It said Barber Lake is “on track” with roughly 95% of long-lead equipment secured, while Black Pearl remains on schedule with engineering, procurement and construction underway.

body_text: Insight M’s methane detection expertise combined with Zeitview’s predictive asset health strengthens an end-to-end critical infrastructure offering for the AI era Los Angeles, CA — February 11, 2026 — Zeitview, the leader in AI-driven asset intelligence for critical infrastructure, today announced that it has acquired Insight M, a leading methane detection and analytics company trusted by the largest oil and gas operators in the world. Uniquely, Zeitview now serves all key sources of energy generation (wind, solar, oil, gas), distribution, and consumption (commercial/industrial facilities, data centers). The acquisition marks Zeitview’s entry into the oil and gas sector and significantly expands the company’s ability to help operators maximize the return, reliability, and predictability of diverse energy assets, while supporting efforts to reduce emissions. Industry data shows that most methane emissions come from a small percentage of assets, where a few large leaks drive disproportionate product loss, operational risk, and regulatory exposure. Historically, operators lacked scalable tools to reliably identify these high-impact events, relying on legacy labor-intensive manual leak detection that couldn’t keep pace with the scale of modern energy systems. The oil and natural gas industry manages millions of miles of pipelines and hundreds of thousands of production facilities. Traditional manual leak detection and repair (LDAR) services alone have proven costly and ineffective in managing emissions from this vast infrastructure. Insight M was built to solve this problem, pioneering large-scale, aircraft-based methane detection to rapidly identify emissions and prioritize repairs with the greatest economic and environmental return. Over the past decade, Insight M has helped operators save approximately $900 million in product value and prevent more than 255 billion cubic feet of methane from entering the atmosphere, among the largest real-world methane mitigation efforts to date. “Insight M has built deep expertise in helping oil and gas companies identify and prioritize high-impact emissions events at basin scale,” said Dan Burton, Founder and CEO of Zeitview. “By combining that capability with Zeitview’s global inspection operations, AI-driven asset intelligence, and visual data platform, we can help operators move from reactive response to proactive asset management, keeping more oil and gas in the pipeline, improving uptime, and making better decisions across their infrastructure. With Insight M as our foundation, our intent is to build something truly unique and complete across visual data for the oil and gas industry.” The acquisition is particularly timely as energy systems face increasing pressure to deliver reliable, predictable supply alongside rising expectations for emissions intensity and environmental performance. The expansion of LNG export capacity and the growing role of natural gas in supporting data centers are accelerating the need for near-zero emissions operations, while optimizing asset performance and operational resilience. The resulting end-to-end, AI-enabled offering will support some of the world’s largest and most sophisticated oil and gas operators, including Occidental Petroleum, BP, and Targa, while building on Zeitview’s existing support for renewable energy assets representing hundreds of gigawatts of capacity, delivering unparalleled scale and coverage for increasingly diversified energy asset portfolios. “This is a natural next chapter for Insight M. Our mission has always been to help operators detect, understand, and reduce methane emissions, but real impact requires context across the entire asset," said David Bercovich, Insight M CEO. "By joining forces with Zeitview, we’re able to expand our capabilities into a more holistic asset integrity platform, one that helps oil and gas customers manage risk, improve performance, and operate more sustainably.” As part of Zeitview, Insight M’s customers will benefit from global scale, an expanded path from methane detection to broader asset intelligence, and the reliability of a cross-industry leader in visual inspection intelligence. Zeitview operates in 80+ countries and brings a proven platform that integrates visual inspections, AI-driven analytics, and human expertise to deliver decision-ready insights at scale. Together, the companies will enable oil and gas operators, as well as diversified, multi-asset owners spanning energy, utilities, and infrastructure, to move toward a more holistic, predictive approach to asset health suited to the demands of modern, AI-driven infrastructure. “The combination of Zeitview and Insight M creates an industry leading asset intelligence platform for energy infrastructure globally,” said Jake van Koevering, Partner at Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT Fund, who will join Zeitview’s Board of Directors. “As the complexity and criticality of power generation increases, we expect Zeitview and Insight M’s comprehensive offering to create deeper relationships with customers and significant long-term impact.” Intrepid Partners, LLC acted as exclusive financial advisor to Insight M, and Fenwick served as legal counsel to Insight M, and Prospera Law LLP served as legal counsel to Zeitview, in connection with the transaction. Zeitview provides full lifecycle asset analytics and visualization, helping the world’s largest enterprises prevent catastrophic failures, predict risk, and optimize maintenance spend across their portfolios. With more than 200,000 assets inspected in over 80 countries, Zeitview enables owners and operators to reduce risk, streamline operations, and make smarter capital allocation decisions. title: Android CI Build Performance — Faster I/O, Faster Builds
summary: It’s not always easy maintaining and improving Android builds, especially as projects continue to grow over time. At Life360, we were…
body_text: Android App Development Android Build System Ci Cd Pipeline Android Gradle Android CI Build Performance — Faster I/O, Faster Builds Pablo Baxter 5 min read · Feb 9, 2026 -- Press enter or click to view image in full size Photo by benjamin lehman on Unsplash It’s not always easy maintaining and improving Android builds, especially as projects continue to grow over time. At Life360, we were looking at our continuous integration (CI) run times, which were averaging ~24 minutes on every pull request. There was an effort to try and reduce this by optimizing JVM flags, optimizing dependency downloads, re-writing the Gradle build-logic, and bringing in Develocity to identify other areas of improvement. Eventually we found that one of the biggest bottlenecks in our Android build was I/O. Identifying the Bottleneck To better explain why I/O is such a bottleneck, let’s dive a little bit into how Android builds APKs and AARs. When an Android binary is built using Gradle, plugins can use process annotations, generate code, bundle assets and resources, transform libraries, and compile Kotlin/Java code. Many of these tasks are cacheable in Gradle, however the Android Gradle Plugin disables caching for tasks that perform I/O only work. Caching I/O only work can have worse performance impact than just re-running the tasks. Press enter or click to view image in full size Before optimizing CI for I/O One thing we noticed was that these tasks took a significant amount of time to run, mainly because there were so many. The image above shows an example of two tasks that correlate to the BundleLibraryClassesDir task and the DataBindingMergeDependencyArtifact task, both of which only perform I/O with hardly any computational work. Yet they each take a non-significant amount of time to run. These tasks are also the longest of these non-cacheable I/O only tasks, with the rest of the 600+ tasks taking 3+ seconds each. Testing a Hypothesis If I/O was faster, our builds should be faster. Obviously increasing memory or processing power won’t improve I/O performance, so we looked at using a different storage medium. Currently, we use AWS instances for our CI pipeline, which we are able to swap for other instances with relative ease. We identified two instances we wanted to test against, one being memory optimized and the other being storage optimized. Due to Android builds being memory hungry, we wanted to prioritize memory over processing power in our benchmarks. We also didn’t want to incur a greater AWS cost, so we chose instances that were about the same price as those we currently used. As for our setup, we used a simple Gradle Profiler scenario that only ran the debug APK assemble task for our Android project. Each run was done in a pipeline we created that allowed us to easily swap out the AWS instance types. We ran five iterations for each instance, with only one warm up run. We first established the baseline of the current instance that ran our build task, which was the m8i.4xlarge instance type. This instance type doesn’t have an SSD, and was using an EBS volume. m8i.4xlarge Results Average time: 514,685.43 ms (~8.6 minutes) This result aligned with what we had seen in our current CI pipelines. Next, we tested the r6idn.2xlarge instance, which is a memory optimized instance that contains a SSD and provided the same amount of memory as the m8i, but had half the number of vCPUs. Although we didn’t want to lose processing power, the cost of the r6idn.4xlarge was almost double of the m8i.4xlarge, so we opted for the reduced number of vCPUs. r6idn.2xlarge Results Average time: 393,328.13 ms (~6.6 minutes) Even with half the number of vCPUs, we saw a 24% improvement over the m8i instance! These I/O only tasks seemed to cause a significant negative impact on our build times. The next instance we tested was the i7i.2xlarge instance, which is a storage optimized instance that had the same amount of vCPUs and memory as the r6idn and was about the same price as well. i7i.2xlarge Results Average time: 289,587.15 ms (~4.8 minutes) The result of the first benchmark was fantastic, however this one was phenomenal! This had a 26% improvement in build performance over the last benchmark, and a >40% improvement over our baseline. When the results were reconfirmed in another round of tests, it was clear the i7i instances were going to run our Android CI pipelines. The numbers are the average time for each phase of our CI. They range about 6 months before we swapped to the i7i instances, and were actually trending towards a positive improvement at the time due to some of the work mentioned earlier (JVM flag fine-tuning and Gradle build-logic re-write). The right side of the graphs capture of CI run times from just before the i7i deployment, up until the end of January. Not only were the improvements clearly visible in these charts, the Android team at Life360 noticed them in their day to day almost immediately as well. In summary, just as the Block and Peloton teams have also found, it is clear that I/O is a significant bottleneck with Android builds on CI. Whether the AWS i7i instances are the best choice for Android builds isn’t as clear though. Additional investigations, analysis, and benchmarking would be necessary to answer that. (the “Company”) (Nasdaq: LECO) today reported fourth quarter 2025 net income of $136.0 million, or diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.45, which includes special item after-tax net charges of $10.6 million, or $0.20 EPS. This compares with prior year period net income of $140.2 million, or $2.47 EPS, which included special item after-tax net charges of $5.8 million, or $0.10 EPS. Excluding special items, fourth quarter 2025 adjusted net income was $146.6 million, or $2.65 adjusted EPS. This compares with adjusted net income of $146.0 million, or $2.57 adjusted EPS, in the prior year period. Fourth quarter 2025 sales increased 5.5% to $1,078.7 million reflecting a 2.5% increase in organic sales, a 1.1% benefit from acquisitions and a 1.9% favorable foreign exchange. Operating income for the fourth quarter 2025 was $184.3 million, or 17.1% of sales. This compares with operating income of $177.0 million, or 17.3% of sales, in the prior year period. Excluding special items, adjusted operating income was $193.8 million, or 18.0% of sales, as compared with $185.6 million, or 18.2% of sales, in the prior year period. “We finished the year with strong results and record sales, adjusted EPS and cash returns to shareholders in 2025,” said Steven B. Hedlund, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. “We are effectively navigating a dynamic operating environment by capitalizing on growth opportunities, mitigating costs, and reshaping the business to extend our leadership position,” Hedlund commented. “We are looking ahead to driving growth, higher profitability and returns as we execute on our new RISE strategy and achieve our 2030 targets.” Twelve Months 2025 Summary Net income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was $520.5 million, or $9.32 EPS, which includes special item after-tax net charges of $30.8 million, or $0.55 EPS. This compares with prior year period net income of $466.1 million, or $8.15 EPS, which included special item after-tax net charges of $65.2 million, or $1.14 EPS. Excluding special items, adjusted net income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was $551.3 million, or $9.87 EPS. This compares with adjusted net income of $531.3 million, or $9.29 adjusted EPS, in the prior year period. Sales increased 5.6% to $4,233.0 million in the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 primarily reflecting a 2.5% increase in organic sales and a 2.7% benefit from acquisitions. Operating income for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 was $718.1 million, or 17.0% of sales. This compares with operating income of $636.5 million, or 15.9% of sales, in the prior year period. Excluding special items, adjusted operating income was $743.0 million, or 17.6% of sales, as compared with $704.4 million, or 17.6% of sales, in the prior year period. Webcast Information A conference call to discuss fourth quarter and full year 2025 financial results as well as new strategic 2030 targets will be webcast live today, February 12, 2026, at 10:00 a.m., Eastern Time. Those interested in participating via webcast in listen-only mode can access the event here or on the Company's Investor Relations home page at https://ir.lincolnelectric.com . For participants who would like to participate via telephone, please dial (888) 440-4368 (domestic) or (646) 960-0856 (international) and use confirmation code 6709091. A replay of the earnings call will be available via webcast on the Company's website. About Lincoln Electric Lincoln Electric is a high-performance industrial machinery and technology leader who helps customers manufacture and maintain vital equipment and infrastructure. Lincoln Electric’s innovative solutions enable higher quality and productivity across a variety of processes including welding, cutting, brazing, machining, process automation and field repair. The Company leverages proprietary technologies and expertise in materials science, power electronics, automation and intelligent software to help customers build better and achieve resilience in their operations. Headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, Lincoln Electric is the essential ‘Linc’ that keeps the economy running. The Company operates 71 manufacturing and automation facilities across 20 countries and serves customers in over 160 countries. For more information about Lincoln Electric and its products and services, visit the Company’s website at https://www.lincolnelectric.com .
